## Task and purpose
- **Task:** The Mini sends Linux-safe tickets to mac-mini-2012. The box builds each one in a fresh `marvin-build` VM, with the bot token and a Claude login handed in on stdin, and the Mac settles the outcome like any other run.
- **Purpose:** a third build lane that uses no Mac capacity, under ADR 0069: disposable VM, credential per run, trust ramp.
- **North star:** work gets done without the owner chasing it, cheaply and within budget.

Closes #951. Part of #949. **Stacked on #969** (#950, the image), which is stacked on #942. The bot's trust ramp is #956 (on main). The marvin opt-in is the-owner/marvin-instance#9.

## How it works
- **Routing** (`box_build.routes`, called by `ticket_pipeline._dispatch_one` before the Macs). A ticket goes to the box only when all of these hold:
  - the project's profile has `"linux_ok": true` (marvin only, instance#9);
  - the ticket is labelled `linux-ok`;
  - no label, title or body word names a macOS thing (Swift, Xcode, launchd, plist, keychain, the dashboard, Electron, vitest, iOS, ...). This fails closed;
  - the box's registry entry accepts `box-build`;
  - the lane isn't resting;
  - the box is online;
  - the one slot is free;
  - this Mac holds the bot token and a login.

  Otherwise the ticket goes to the Macs exactly as before. Any error in routing means "Macs".
- **Claim** `claimed:mac-mini-2012` (`_label_for_device` no longer maps the box to the M4 Mini's `mac-mini`). Then `box_build.py run` starts detached on the Mac. The box host never runs a ticket itself, and there is no fallback to it.
- **Secrets.** The bot token (`~/.claude/.marvin-bot-token`) and the login travel only on ssh's stdin. The remote command line holds names and numbers only, all validated (ticket ref, 40-hex engine SHA, run id, `$HOME`-safe path). vm_run exports them for the one command in the VM. Output is scrubbed of both values on the box and again on the Mac before any log.
- **Login, plan first** (the `builder_auth.sh` rule). The plan's OAuth token is used while a box plan slot is free. The API key only for a build beyond the plan slots, only with `credit_slots["mac-mini-2012"] > 0` and the credit ready. The box has one slot and no credit slots, so it always uses the plan. Each choice goes to `builder-billing.jsonl`.
- **In the VM.** It checks the bot token with `gh api user` (a rejection is a refusal, not a ticket failure), checks out the Mac's engine commit, then runs `run_ticket.py --build-only`: execute_ticket → raise_mr, pushing as the bot with a noreply identity. It prints one `MARVIN_BUILD_OUTCOME` line.
- **On the Mac.** `run_ticket.settle()` (split out of `run()`; `run()` = build + settle, unchanged for the Macs) does the comment, claim, stage, breaker and redispatch. On a raised PR, the Mac adds the `from-box` label and a comment with the run's numbers.
- **One at a time.**
  - `config/dispatch.json` `box_builds.slots` is 0 or 1, validated and enforced by `dispatch_concurrency.can_start_box_build`.
  - A non-blocking `flock` on the box means two dispatchers racing get "busy".
  - Box builds count in `running_tickets` for `max_total` / `max_per_project`.
- **Guards on the box**, before any VM: memory (`MemAvailable - memory_mb >= reserve_mb`), VM disk free `>= guards.min_disk_gb`, golden image present, and a `vm_run.sweep()` of anything a crash left. A box build doesn't mark the box busy, so its test and trial work keep queuing.
- **Failure.**
  - Busy, memory, disk, no image, missing secret, rejected token or bad engine commit: the claim goes back with no strike.
  - A hang, the VM timing out, the box dropping off, no result, or the Mac-side runner being stopped: run_ticket's timed-out path (no strike, retry with backoff, capped). These also feed the failure breaker (#881's rule).
  - Both kinds rest the lane (`box-lane.json`: 10 min for memory up to 6 h for a rejected token), so a broken box can't fail every ticket in turn.
  - The Mac holds ssh's stdin open for the whole run. When the Mac goes away the box reads EOF and destroys the VM (found live, below).
- **ADR 0069 amendment 2** records all of this.

## Live proof: PR #984, built end to end in a box VM

## Found live and fixed in this PR
Live runs on #870 (a real `ready-for-agent` Python ticket), each in a fresh VM:

| Run | Wall | Peak VM RSS | Host peak used / min available | Ended | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 86 s | 2.9 GB | 4.7 / 11.2 GB | baseline: `test_find_file` imports from the private `~/.claude` | the test skips without it; the VM ignores that one file in baseline and verify alike |
| 2 | 1260 s | 3.4 GB | 5.3 / 10.6 GB | baseline: serial suite at 63 % after 1200 s | pytest `-n <vCPUs>` in the VM, 6 vCPUs |
| 3 | 516 s | 5.3 GB | 7.2 / 8.7 GB | planner crashed reading the memory index (no `~/.claude` in a VM, by design) | `marvin_launcher` leaves out missing private layers |
| 4 | 1427 s | 5.4 GB | 7.6 / 8.3 GB | planner hit 900 s (Mini median 405 s, p90 606 s) | `MARVIN_STEP_TIMEOUT_SCALE`, 2.5 in the VM; box run limit 9000 s |
| 5 | 556 s | 5.5 GB | 7.4 / 8.5 GB | the plan's 5-hour limit | none needed: model-unavailable, released, no strike |
| **6** | **3680 s** | **6.2 GB** | **8.2 / 7.7 GB** | **PR #984 raised as `the-bot`**, labelled `from-box`, with the run comment | its commit still names the owner as author (`mr_raiser` hard-codes it): fixed here, a box build now commits as the bot |

Also checked live:
- **Killing the Mac-side runner** left the box building. Fixed: stdin stays open and EOF tears the VM down.
- **Dropping the link mid-boot** (dummy secrets): the VM, disk and owner record were gone within 12 s.
- **A preflight VM** with the real secrets on stdin: `gh api user` → `the-bot`, context for every launch kind, `claude -p` on the plan login → `ok`.
- **After every run**, `virsh list --all` showed only the Whonix pair and `runs/` held only `golden/`.
- **Billing:** every run logged `mode: plan, why: plan-slot`.

Peak memory with a 6144 MB VM: 6.2 GB RSS at most, host at most 8.2 of 15.9 GB used, at least 7.7 GB left for the box's own test and trial work.

The failed runs touched #870: two strikes and a park, which I undid with a comment explaining that the failures were this lane's. #870 keeps `claimed:mac-mini-2012` while PR #984 is open, like any raised ticket. **PR #984 is not merged.**

## Tests
New or extended:
- `test_box_build.py` (100);
- `test_run_ticket.py` (build/settle split, `--build-only`);
- `test_ticket_pipeline.py` (box route, claim and release, lost race, macOS ticket to a Mac, crashing router, dry run);
- `test_running_tickets.py`, `test_dispatch_concurrency.py` (through `box_build`), `test_marvin_launcher.py`, `test_sandbox_orchestration.py`.

How they try to break it:
- secrets in argv, the remote command, logs, the billing log and the result, including a build that echoes them;
- injection through the ticket ref, the engine SHA, the run id, the box engine path and the worker count;
- the VM hanging, ssh timing out, exit 255, no or garbled result, a fake PR link;
- a bot token missing, multi-line or rejected;
- two builds racing for the flock;
- 11 macOS-shaped tickets labelled `linux-ok`, plus words that only contain a Mac word;
- a crash, a stop or a settle failure in the runner;
- a corrupt lane file, dead runner records;
- a $HOME without `~/.claude`.

Full suite: see the comment below.

## Decisions
<!-- marvin:decisions -->
### routing-signal: What sends a ticket to the box
- [x] The `linux-ok` label, set by you or triage (as built: explicit, fails closed)
- [ ] Automatic for tickets whose text names only Python, docs or config, still with the macOS-word check

### order: When a ticket can go to either
- [x] The box first while its slot is free (as built: frees the Macs and earns the bot's trust ramp)
- [ ] The Macs first; the box only when they are full

### vm-size: Box build VM size and limits
- [x] 6144 MB, 6 vCPUs, 9000 s, 3072 MB kept free (as built, from the live runs above)
- [ ] Smaller: 4096 MB, 4 vCPUs, so a test run always fits beside it

### private-context: What a box VM knows
- [x] No private memory, work rules or lexicon: only the repo and the ticket (as built)
- [ ] Hand in the work-rule notes on stdin per run too
> **Note:** The VM box when testing Marvin should be using our default build that we're using here soon and then it can configure it to whatever tools we have that we need to build for it for whatever task project it is.
